title: vet-flat evidence
description: Part of Pea Princess (vet-flat) by Hsien Hao (Jacky) Chen - https://github.com/jacky18008/pea-princess - CC BY 4.0. What the executors write in the role pipeline (references/pipeline.md): one item per thing that was read, and nothing else. NO VERDICTS. NO SCORES. NO ARITHMETIC except a scripts/calc.py call recorded in computed_by. An executor that could not get something writes an item with status "unknown" and lists what it tried, because a gap somebody tried to fill is a different thing from a gap nobody looked at. Every found item carries a verbatim quote and a source that resolves, and scripts/verify.py checks both.

case.description: The same short label the plan carries.

flat.description: The flat this run is about, as the register writes it: "301", "12b". The referent guard needs it to tell this flat's numbers from the one next door.

group.description: The executor group that wrote this file, when one executor writes its own. The harness merges the groups.

items.description: One item per fact. Two executors may write about the same axis; ids must still be unique across the merged file.

id.description: A short id unique in this file, for example "e1". The verifier reports on it and the report cites it.

axis.description: The axis this belongs to, 1 to 12, as in report-schema.json.

claim.description: What this number or fact IS, in plain words: "certified internal floor area", "police recorded crimes in the standard box over six months". This is what the referent guard reads, so name the thing, not the source.

status.description: ok = it was read and the quote is below. unknown = it could not be got; say what was tried in `tried`, and leave value, quote and source out.

value.description: The value exactly as the source states it. A number stays a number; a letter grade or a class name is a string. Never a range, never a rounded figure, never a guess.

unit.description: The unit, written out: "m2", "square feet", "minutes", "GBP per month", "crimes per six months", "weeks of rent". A number without a unit is not evidence; scripts/verify.py fails it.

source.description: Either an id that resolves in the report's sources[] ("epc-cert"), or "pasted:<name>" for text the user supplied, where <name> is the file in the pasted-sources folder. Never "the internet", never a bare URL with no entry behind it.

quote.description: The sentence you read it in, VERBATIM, copied not retyped. scripts/verify.py looks for it in the source, ignoring only how the whitespace falls. At most 300 characters, the same limit as the report.

fetched_at.description: When it was read, UTC, as 2026-09-06T11:20:00Z. Crime counts and journey times move.

script.description: The exact command that produced it, when a script did: "scripts/epc.py cert 1234-5678-9012-3456-7890". Blank when the text was pasted.

computed_by.description: The ONLY arithmetic an executor may report, and only as a scripts/calc.py call with its output: "calc.py deposit --rent-pcm 2400 -> 5 weeks = 2769.23". Anything an executor worked out in its head belongs to nobody and is thrown away.

tried.description: For an unknown item: what was actually attempted, one line each, specific enough for somebody else to carry on. An unknown with an empty `tried` is a gap nobody looked at, and scripts/verify.py --strict fails it.

note.description: Anything the verifier should know: that the register carries two flats at this number, that the month is missing rather than zero.
